knowledge:
- key_parameters: subset.row=Specifies the subset of genes (typically highly variable genes) to restrict the velocity calculations to ;; assay.X=The assay name or index to use as the exonic expression proxy (typically "spliced" or exonic counts) ;; scvelo.params=A named list of arguments passed to individual scvelo Python functions (e.g., list(neighbors=list(n_neighbors=30L)) or list(recover_dynamics=list(max_iter=20))) ;; use.dimred=Pre-computed dimensionality reduction coordinates (e.g., "PCA") to bypass scvelo's internal PCA step and ensure consistency ;; use.theirs=Logical; if TRUE, uses the default scvelo pipeline without modification, ignoring subset.row and using scvelo's internal normalization/feature selection
- alternatives: Pure Python-based scvelo analysis (can be mimicked using use.theirs=TRUE but sacrifices consistency with Bioconductor workflows)
- when_to_use: When analyzing single-cell RNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced count matrices to estimate transcriptional dynamics (RNA velocity) within a Bioconductor/SingleCellExperiment framework.
- pitfalls: Memory usage: The full dataset can require up to 12 GB of memory ;; Neighbor calculation: Automatic neighbor calculation is deprecated in scvelo >= 0.4.0. Users should supply the number of neighbors to scanpy.pp.neighbors via scvelo.params=list(neighbors=list(n_neighbors=30L)) to reproduce older results (default was 30 for scvelo.pp.moments but is 15 for scanpy.pp.neighbors) ;; Spliced vs. Exonic counts: Using "spliced" counts as a proxy for exonic counts is generally satisfactory but has subtle differences (see ?scvelo for details)

workflows.name: rna_velocity_scvelo
workflows.intent: Calculate RNA velocity from spliced and unspliced single-cell RNA-seq counts, project the velocity vectors onto a low-dimensional embedding, and visualize the grid-summarized velocity vectors.
workflows.stages: 1. Feature selection (identifying highly variable genes using scran) ;; 2. RNA velocity estimation using scvelo() ;; 3. Dimensionality reduction (PCA and t-SNE) ;; 4. Velocity embedding projection using embedVelocity() ;; 5. Grid-based summarization of velocity vectors using gridVectors() ;; 6. Visualization of velocity pseudotime and vectors using ggplot2
workflows.code:
library(scRNAseq)
sce <- HermannSpermatogenesisData()
sce

sce <- sce[, 1:500]

library(scuttle)
sce <- logNormCounts(sce, assay.type=1)

library(scran)
dec <- modelGeneVar(sce)
top.hvgs <- getTopHVGs(dec, n=2000)

library(velociraptor)
velo.out <- scvelo(
  sce, subset.row=top.hvgs, assay.X="spliced",
  scvelo.params=list(neighbors=list(n_neighbors=30L))
)
velo.out

library(scater)

set.seed(100)
sce <- runPCA(sce, subset_row=top.hvgs)
sce <- runTSNE(sce, dimred="PCA", perplexity = 30)

sce$velocity_pseudotime <- velo.out$velocity_pseudotime
plotTSNE(sce, colour_by="velocity_pseudotime")

embedded <- embedVelocity(reducedDim(sce, "TSNE"), velo.out)
grid.df <- gridVectors(sce, embedded, use.dimred = "TSNE")

library(ggplot2)
plotTSNE(sce, colour_by="velocity_pseudotime") +
    geom_segment(data=grid.df, mapping=aes(x=start.1, y=start.2, 
        xend=end.1, yend=end.2, colour=NULL), arrow=arrow(length=unit(0.05, "inches")))
